entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Leodegar of Poitiers was a martyred Burgundian Bishop of Autun. He was the son of Saint Sigrada and the brother of Saint Warinus.

Born around 635 AD, Leodegar rose to prominence as Bishop of Autun during the tumultuous Merovingian period. His appointment was a strategic move by the Frankish king Theudebert III to consolidate power and counterbalance the influence of the Burgundians.

In 678, Leodegar was martyred during the Frankish conquest of Burgundy, leading to the eventual incorporation of Burgundian territory into the Frankish Empire. His death marked the end of Burgundian independence and had far-reaching consequences for the regional balance of power.

Despite his relatively short tenure as Bishop, Leodegar's legacy as a martyr and a symbol of Burgundian resistance to Frankish rule endured, shaping the identity of the Burgundians and their place in medieval history.

The impact of Leodegar's martyrdom can still be seen today in the cultural and historical landscape of Burgundy and beyond, a testament to the enduring power of faith and resistance in the face of overwhelming force.
